name: TCA (citric acid / Krebs) cycle
summary: In the mitochondrial matrix, acetyl-CoA is oxidised to 2 CO₂. Each turn captures the released energy as 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 GTP; oxaloacetate is regenerated. The cycle also supplies biosynthetic precursors (citrate, α-ketoglutarate, succinyl-CoA, oxaloacetate).
location: Mitochondrial matrix (succinate dehydrogenase in the inner membrane)
net: Acetyl-CoA + 3 NAD⁺ + FAD + GDP + Pᵢ + 2 H₂O → 2 CO₂ + 3 NADH + FADH₂ + GTP + CoA + 3 H⁺
clinical: Mutations in succinate dehydrogenase (SDHx) and fumarate hydratase cause hereditary paraganglioma and renal cancer; IDH1/2 mutations produce the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (glioma, AML; ivosidenib/enasidenib).

references.label: Berg et al., Biochemistry 5th ed., ch. 17 (NCBI Bookshelf)

enzyme.name: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
enzyme.regulation: Inhibited by PDK phosphorylation, acetyl-CoA, NADH

edges.description: Entry point (not part of the cycle proper). Requires TPP, lipoate, CoA, FAD, NAD⁺.

enzyme.name: Isocitrate dehydrogenase
enzyme.regulation: Activated by ADP, Ca²⁺; inhibited by ATP, NADH

enzyme.name: α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase
enzyme.regulation: Inhibited by succinyl-CoA, NADH; activated by Ca²⁺

edges.description: Substrate-level phosphorylation (GTP-forming isoform; an ADP-forming isoform also exists).
The only TCA enzyme embedded in the inner membrane; passes electrons directly to ubiquinone.
Unfavourable (ΔG°′ ≈ +30 kJ/mol) but pulled forward by rapid consumption of oxaloacetate.
